We have search results: three templates. Need to apply appropriate template to target molecule to get precursors. The target molecule is a sulfonamide with aromatic amine attached to sulfonyl group, plus other substituents: O=S(NC1=...)(C5=...)=O. The template likely matches generic sulfonamide formation: retro_smarts_template: '[O;D1;H0:2]=[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])(-[c:4])-[NH;D2;+0:5]-[c:6]>>O-[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])(=[O;D1;H0:3])-[c:4].[NH2;D1;+0:5]-[c:6]'

This template splits sulfonamide into sulfonyl chloride? Actually product side: O-[S](=O)(=O)-[c] (aryl sulfonyl chloride?) Wait: The left side of ">>" is product (target) and right side are precursors. The retro template: product (sulfonamide) -> precursors: sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and an aniline (aryl amine). The template's right side: O-[S](=O)(=O)-[c:4] . [NH2]-[c:6] . That is sulfonyl chloride? Actually O-[S](=O)(=O)-[c] is sulfonyl chloride? No chlorine not shown. Might be sulfonyl chloride with O? Wait O-[S](=O)(=O)-[c] is sulfonic acid? Hmm.

But we can apply this template to our molecule using apply_template tool with template_id from result. Choose first template (reaction_id 214705). template_hash given. Need template_id? Probably template_hash is ID? The tool get_template expects template_id. The search result includes template_hash. Might be used as template_id. Let's try apply_template with that hash.
